expectations.text: States the change: PCI SSC updated FAQ 1331 on August 31, 2026, restricting this practice
expectations.evidence: "FAQ 1331 (updated August 31, 2026)" — states the update and restriction explicitly

expectations.text: States the new rule: SAQ eligibility criteria may not be used as a guide for ROC requirement applicability unless explicitly reviewed, discussed and agreed with the merchant's compliance accepting entity (payment brands and/or acquirer)
expectations.evidence: quotes rule: SAQ criteria may not guide ROC applicability "unless explicitly reviewed, discussed and agreed upon with the merchant's compliance accepting entity" — "your acquiring bank and/or the relevant card brand(s), not just your QSA"

expectations.text: Makes the key point: QSA agreement alone no longer suffices — acquirer/brand approval is needed
expectations.evidence: "QSA agreement alone is no longer sufficient evidence... You need it 'explicitly reviewed, discussed and agreed upon' with your acquirer and/or card brand"

expectations.text: Identifies who is affected: merchants undergoing ROC assessments (mandatory Level 1 or voluntary), notably e-commerce scoping under requirements like 6.4.3/11.6.1
expectations.evidence: Level 1 merchant "required to complete a full Report on Compliance (ROC)"; "particularly around Req 6.4.3 and 11.6.1" e-commerce scoping

expectations.text: Gives the right advice: obtain and document the acquirer/payment-brand agreement in writing before relying on SAQ-based scope reduction
expectations.evidence: "Get it in writing... obtain documented approval from your acquiring bank... Keep this correspondence as part of your assessment evidence file" before ROC finalization
